rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to retain early compounds while eluting strongly retained ones near the 10-minute scoring target. The retention window and weakest resolutions will guide gradient trimming and temperature optimization.

Change only gradient duration to test whether the crowded middle peaks respond to a shallower slope. The current last peak at 7.16 minutes leaves room to improve resolution without exceeding the 10-minute scoring threshold.

Raise the starting organic fraction slightly to trim unused early gradient time while making the slope shallower at fixed duration. This should further separate the remaining critical pair while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes; the first peak should remain retained.

The critical pair improves with a shallower gradient, so extend the gradient to 16 minutes and raise phi0 to offset the added retention time. This targets R ≥ 1.5 for every pair while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes and preserving early-peak separation.

Injection 4 reached the maximum possible CRF; now test a higher starting organic fraction to shorten elution while retaining that score. The slightly shallower slope should support the critical pair, while the early pair has resolution margin to tolerate some compression.

Return to the fully resolved gradient and increase temperature by 5 °C to test whether elution can be shortened without losing critical-pair resolution. Injection 4 remains the maximum-score fallback.

The critical pair converged strongly between 40 and 45 °C; testing 55 °C may separate it again after an elution-order reversal while shortening retention. Check all adjacent pairs because temperature may introduce a different bottleneck.

Slightly lengthen the gradient to improve the new critical pair, currently at R = 1.41. The last peak at 8.54 minutes leaves room for this change to restore full resolution while remaining below the 10-minute threshold.

Test whether a lower starting organic fraction improves selectivity around the new critical pair enough to use the shorter 16-minute gradient. This should keep the last peak below 10 minutes and may yield a faster fully resolved method than injection 8.

Shorten injection 9’s gradient to seek a faster method with the same maximum CRF. The 55 °C duration comparison suggests the narrowest middle pair may improve slightly with a steeper slope, while the other close pair has resolution margin.

Test a shorter gradient while lowering phi0 to protect the pair that loses resolution as the gradient steepens. Previous runs suggest these changes may balance the two limiting pairs and preserve CRF 1.000 with earlier final elution.

With the maximum CRF already secured, test a cooler selectivity regime for a potentially shorter fully resolved method. Lower temperature may separate the crowded middle peaks differently, while the broad 10-minute gradient should keep final elution near the scoring window.

Test a faster, high-temperature regime where the approaching middle pair may reverse order and regain separation. This is an exploratory attempt to shorten the fully resolved method; injection 11 already provides the maximum CRF at a 7.60-minute last peak.

Test whether raising the starting organic fraction separates the remaining close pair in the reversed-order, high-temperature regime. This may preserve the rapid elution of injection 13, but all neighboring resolutions must be checked for new bottlenecks.

Test whether a steeper gradient increases separation of the reversed-order critical pair at 60 °C while shortening elution further. The neighboring pair at R = 1.62 has little margin, so this run will test the tradeoff rather than assume that faster is better.

Preserve injection 11’s successful slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute while trimming the unused gradient endpoint. Its last peak eluted near phi = 0.57, so all peaks should retain their separation and elute before this shorter programmed gradient ends.

Test an intermediate slope of 0.065 per minute at phi0 = 0.10 to locate the fastest fully resolved boundary in this temperature regime. This should shorten injection 10 while testing whether its R = 1.77 pair retains sufficient resolution.

Test whether lowering phi0 restores the neighboring separation lost in injection 15 while the steeper slope separates the reversed-order critical pair. This explores a faster selectivity window; injection 16 remains a demonstrated maximum-score method.

Increase the slope slightly from the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method, from 0.075 to 0.080 organic fraction per minute. This tests whether the critical pairs retain R ≥ 1.5 while bringing the last peak earlier than 7.60 minutes.

Explore the untested 35 °C selectivity window with a relatively fast gradient, since neither further steepening at 55 °C nor the tested 60 °C methods achieved full resolution. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this run seeks an alternative faster separation rather than a higher possible score.

Test a slightly shallower slope than injection 8 to seek more balanced resolution margins while preserving the maximum CRF. Its last peak at 9.35 minutes leaves some room for added retention without a time penalty.

Test the remaining 50 °C selectivity window with a fast gradient to see whether the crowded middle peaks separate before new co-elutions develop. The campaign already has maximum-score methods, so this is an exploratory search for shorter fully resolved elution.

Test whether a higher starting fraction and shallower slope can balance the two limiting pairs at 50 °C. This explores a potentially faster fully resolved alternative while retaining the already demonstrated maximum-score methods as fallbacks.

Use a slope of 0.0625 per minute, between injections 10 and 17, to balance their two limiting resolutions. This targets a maximum-score method with slightly better resolution margin than the fastest demonstrated method, while keeping final elution near 8 minutes.

Trim injection 24’s unused gradient endpoint while preserving its slope of 0.0625 per minute. Its last peak eluted near phi = 0.56, so this method should preserve CRF 1.000 and the 8.00-minute final elution with a shorter programmed gradient.
